items.text: In early counting from Taiwan's [[e:2026 Taiwanese local elections|local elections]], Reuters reported Taipei mayor [[p:Chiang Wan-an]] of the [[p:Kuomintang]] leading the [[p:Democratic Progressive Party|DPP]]'s [[p:Puma Shen]], whom Beijing says is wanted for separatism. The DPP looked on course to hold Kaohsiung and Tainan and the KMT to hold New Taipei, while the DPP's Ho Hsin-chun narrowly led in Taichung. Taiwan's defence ministry counted 33 Chinese military aircraft and eight warships around the island in the 24 hours before voting.
items.notes: PRELIMINARY: the Reuters count is from about 18:00 local time (10:00 UTC); neither Taipei camp had conceded. Final results were expected before midnight and the CEC formally announces winners on 4 Dec. The Focus Taiwan live page (CNA) had no results when fetched. A nuclear-power referendum was held the same day; no result yet. Military-activity figures are from Reuters, Yahoo copy: https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/taiwan-votes-key-local-elections-000134325.html . Last cycle (2022) the KMT won 14, the DPP 5 and others 3. UPDATE WITH FINAL RESULTS.

items.text: [[p:United States Central Command|US Central Command]] said an aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman after it left Bandar Abbas and tried to run the US blockade of Iranian ports; the crew was unharmed. AP counts it as at least the 15th ship disabled since April. On 27 Nov the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] said a tanker on an 'unauthorised' route hit a mine and exploded and another turned back, and Iran's navy chief said Iran would break the blockade.
items.notes: The IRGC mine claim is unverified. Press TV placed it north of Ghannam Island (Pakistan Today: https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/11/27/irgc-says-tanker-hit-mine-exploded-in-strait-of-hormuz); the 28 Nov Al Jazeera blog says two tankers hit mines near Khasab. The IRGC also claimed warning shots at a US F-16 near Hengam Island. The US says it has redirected 158 ships since July.

items.text: Italian Foreign Minister [[p:Antonio Tajani]] said Kuwaiti investigators found the drone that killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait was made in Iran, while noting that Iran's allies also field Iranian-made drones. Iran denies launching it; Foreign Minister [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] called the attack suspicious, and Tehran has offered to join a joint inquiry with Italy and Kuwait. Saudi Arabia and Syria blamed Iran.
items.notes: Tajani's statement attributes manufacture, not who launched it. Al Jazeera live blog 28 Nov: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/28/iran-war-live-italy-says-drone-in-deadly-kuwait-attack-was-made-in-iran

items.text: [[p:Donald Trump]] publicly backed Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi's drive to stop oil smuggling and put all weapons under state control. During the week Baghdad moved to put the Kurdistan Region's border crossings and several oilfields under federal control and closed two crossings, one to Syria and one to Iran. Iraq's top court ruled that federal forces can deploy on all borders, including the Kurdish region's. The [[p:Kurdistan Regional Government]] called this a breach of its constitutional rights but said it does not want clashes, and thousands protested on 26 Nov.
items.notes: No independent second link was fetched (web-search budget exhausted, Rudaw blocked). Al-Zaidi had earlier ordered the army to prepare to enter Jurf al-Sakhar, held by Kataib Hezbollah. A Baghdad–Erbil meeting under the Supreme Judicial Council head is set for 1 Dec. Baghdad estimates it lost about $100bn to smuggling in 2008–25; Reuters says how that figure was calculated is unclear.

items.text: [[p:Médecins Sans Frontières|MSF]] said an Israeli strike directly hit its clearly marked clinic in Gaza City on the night of 27 Nov, killing two staff guards. It said the clinic's location was known to the Israeli military and that 17 of its staff have now been killed in Gaza. The Israeli military said the two were Hamas members but gave no evidence. WHO chief [[p:Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus]] called the strike unacceptable.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: Al Jazeera dates it to 'Friday' night, which is 27 Nov. Sourced to MSF's post on X; no independent second outlet was fetched (msf.org blocked). On 27 Nov Al Jazeera also reported four killed in Gaza and a strike that the son of Hamas leader al-Hayya survived.

items.text: National Assembly head Jorge Rodríguez said Venezuela will repeal the 2024 law used to bar opposition figures who backed sanctions from holding office, one of the laws flagged for review in the US-backed transition talks. [[p:María Corina Machado]], who was excluded from the talks, launched neighbourhood assemblies to draft a government programme. Her team said about 2,000 met on day one. No election date has been set.
items.notes: The repeal's timing and mechanism were not given. Repeal would remove a legal bar Machado faced. No independent second link was fetched.

items.text: The [[p:Islamabad High Court]] heard defence arguments in the appeals of [[p:Imran Khan]] and [[p:Bushra Bibi]] against their Al-Qadir Trust (£190m) convictions. Counsel Salman Safdar argued that no money reached either defendant's personal accounts and that the state suffered no loss. The bench reserved its decision on a request to live-stream the appeals and adjourned until next week without setting a date.
items.notes: The Islamabad advocate general told the court Bushra Bibi now has a separate room and filed her medical records for April–21 Nov. Latif Khosa asked for the couple to be allowed to meet before the next hearing; the court said it would issue an order. Neither report mentions Imran Khan's health. In a 16 Nov open letter Khan said his blood pressure had reached 193; the government disputes this (Dawn).

items.text: Police stopped [[p:Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F)|JUI-F]] chief Fazlur Rehman from leaving Lahore for a party rally in Sargodha by putting containers around his home, according to the party. He then called nationwide protests, and his workers blocked motorways and highways. The government told the [[p:Lahore High Court]] he had not been detained. On 27 Nov Fazl ended the road sit-ins but kept protests after Friday prayers, and Information Minister [[p:Attaullah Tarar]] told him to choose between Pakistan and the Taliban.
items.notes: Claims of house arrests (Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, Punjab chief Amjad Khan) and a worker being tortured come from Fazl and were not independently confirmed. The ending of the sit-ins is from PakWheels (https://www.pakwheels.com/blog/jui-f-calls-off-motorway-sit-ins-friday-protests/). Afghanistan International gives only a summary of Tarar's remark; the full context was not available.

items.text: Pakistan hosted the second meeting of the strategic committee set up under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed on 7 Aug. Their foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs, including [[p:Asim Munir]], [[p:Khalid bin Salman]] and [[p:Hakan Fidan]], condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and pledged to step up support. They announced no new military measures. Turkey's president approved the pact the same day, completing Turkish ratification, AP reported.
items.notes: The parties call the pact defensive and say it targets no country. Retired Pakistani Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood is its first secretary-general, and its secretariat is in Saudi Arabia (Pakistan Today: https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/11/28/pm-reaffirms-pakistans-firm-commitment-to-makkah-defence-alliance).

items.text: Iran's Foreign Minister [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] told state TV that Pakistani and Qatari mediators are still carrying proposals between Tehran and Washington. He said Iran would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its conditions are met: an end to the US naval blockade, an end to the war on all fronts, and sanctions relief. The same day [[p:Ishaq Dar]] spoke to Araghchi, who invited Pakistan to an ECO summit on 3–4 Dec.
items.notes: Washington wants assurances on safe passage and wants Iran's nuclear programme included in initial talks (Arab News). No second independent source was read for the interview.

items.text: The [[p:Balochistan Liberation Army]] claimed that drone and ground attacks on a Frontier Corps camp at Hazhda Khol in Nushki on 21 Nov, and on reinforcement convoys and troops in Nushki and Mastung, killed 20 security personnel; it also claimed attacks in Chagai, Buleda and Qilla Abdullah on 22 Nov. Pakistan has not commented on the claim. The military's [[p:Inter-Services Public Relations|ISPR]] said on 26 Nov that troops killed 12 militants in Noshki, Sibi, Panjgur and Kech between 20 and 23 Nov, eight of them at a hideout in Noshki on 20 Nov, and reported no army losses.
items.notes: The two accounts conflict and neither has been verified independently. The BLA's itemised figures do not clearly add up to 20. ISPR calls the militants India-sponsored; India denies backing them. IANS relies on a BLA statement carried by The Balochistan Post.

items.text: The Balochistan Post, cited by IANS, reported that a bomb and gun attack on a military convoy in the Bil Nagor area of Kech district killed four soldiers and wounded seven. The military has not confirmed the toll, and no group had claimed the attack.
items.notes: Early reports gave two dead and five wounded.

items.text: Gunmen shot dead Kamran Mehsud, the officer in charge of Sarokai police station, in Dera Ismail Khan and wounded two passers-by. On 22 Nov the army and the Counter-Terrorism Department killed three suspected [[p:Pakistani Taliban]] militants in a raid in Peshawar's Matni area, police said.
items.notes: Minute Mirror counts six police and security personnel killed in Dera Ismail Khan, Tank and South Waziristan between 30 Oct and 25 Nov. The 24NewsHD Peshawar report is by Ahmad Mansoor.

items.text: ARY News, citing unnamed sources, reported that the federal government is considering extending governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by two months. It was imposed on 11 Oct and its first two-month term ends on 11 Dec. An extension needs a resolution at a joint sitting of Parliament, and the constitution caps the total at six months. Officials are also weighing whether to keep the emergency in eight former tribal districts and four settled districts.
items.notes: The deposed PTI chief minister Sohail Afridi has been in custody since 11 Oct; petitions over his detention and the emergency are pending before the PHC and the Federal Constitutional Court (Dawn, 12 Nov: https://www.dawn.com/news/2044048/pti-lawmaker-moves-fcc-seeking-immediate-release-of-sohail-afridi-other-party-workers). There is no on-record government statement on an extension.

items.text: Sources told Afghanistan International that Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al-Khulaifi is due in Kabul and Islamabad from 28 Nov, then Uzbekistan, to revive Qatari mediation between Pakistan and the Taliban. Trade and transport links are also expected to come up. Qatar has not commented.
items.notes: Qatar and Turkey brokered the October 2025 Doha ceasefire. Torkham and Chaman have been closed to regular trade since October 2025. Separately, the British High Commission said UK army chief Gen Roly Walker met Asim Munir on 25 Nov and visited a Pakistani post on the Afghan border (Khaama Press: https://www.khaama.com/uk-army-chief-pakistan-afghanistan-border-visit/).

items.text: The [[p:International Monetary Fund|IMF]] has scheduled its board meeting on Pakistan for 11 Dec. The meeting covers the Article IV consultation, the fourth review of the $7bn Extended Fund Facility and the third review of the climate facility, and approval would release about $1.21bn. Weekly SPI inflation fell to 9.49% year on year in the week to 26 Nov, down from 10.41% the week before, though wheat flour is up about 54% on a year earlier.
items.notes: This replaces the 9 Dec date in watch item W-261121-03. 24NewsHD calls the $1bn EFF portion the fifth tranche. SPI figures are from the Express Tribune: https://tribune.com.pk/story/2642703/spi-inflation-moderates-to-single-digits.

items.text: [[p:Bilawal Bhutto Zardari]] said in Rahim Yar Khan that he rejects dividing Punjab into four provinces but backs a South Punjab province. It is the latest step in the PPP's dispute with its PML-N-led coalition partners over federal ministers' proposals for new provinces. In speeches this month he has also opposed a referendum on the issue and urged the government to return PTI's reserved seats and electoral symbol.
items.notes: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif have floated new administrative units, with Asif suggesting up to 12 (Dawn, 17 Nov). A Nation editorial on 27 Nov read Bilawal's Multan remarks as a softer but still pressing line on the government.

items.text: Taliban forces shot dead six men from Panjshir at a checkpoint in Kabul's Karte Naw area. A Kabul police spokesman said the men were armed thieves killed in a gunfight after ignoring orders to stop. Sources and a relative told KabulNow the men had not seen the signal and were shot after their car caught fire, and that the bodies were handed back only once families agreed not to publicise the case.
items.notes: The accounts conflict, and neither has been verified independently. KabulNow named five of the dead.

items.text: The Taliban's vice-and-virtue department in Nangarhar said it had collected and burned more than 1,600 musical instruments taken in Kama, Kuz Kunar and Dara-e Noor districts, along with confiscated fireworks. Earlier this year Khost burned 650 instruments and Logar nearly 200.

The Taliban's National Development Corporation said excavation of the second phase of the [[p:Qosh Tepa Canal]] is 99% complete and Amu Darya water will soon flow into it. Uzbekistan's water minister said on 19 Nov that the canal will not draw water before 2030 and that withdrawals must be negotiated, while acknowledging Afghanistan's right to use the river.
items.notes: The Taliban put the cost at about $680m; a 2019 feasibility study estimated about $1.5bn for the main canal.

items.text: The Union Cabinet chaired by [[p:Narendra Modi]] approved a new constitutional amendment bill that would tie one-third reservation for women to delimitation, enlarging every state's [[p:Lok Sabha]] seats by 50% while freezing each state's share of seats until 2051. Parliament has been called for a special sitting from 30 Nov, and Parliamentary Affairs Minister [[p:Kiren Rijiju]] said the bill would be introduced that day. An earlier delimitation amendment fell short of a two-thirds majority in April (298–230).
items.notes: Opposition parties back women's reservation but object to delimitation and say they have not seen the bill text. DMK chief Stalin wants Tamil Nadu's share kept at 7.18% or above. NCP-SP has offered support. Congress floor leaders were due to meet on 28 Nov. Reports differ on the new maximum size of the House (about 815 vs about 850).

items.text: A [[p:Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] bench found a prima facie case of wilful disobedience by Tamil Nadu officials and the trustees of the Thiruparankundram temple after the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon was not lit on 24 Nov, despite a 20 Nov order allowing a one-time lighting. The court replaced the trustees with two former High Court judges, handed hill security to the [[p:Central Reserve Police Force]], ordered the lamp lit on 28 Nov and listed the case for 15 Dec. The bench said authorities had acted on instructions from their political superiors.
items.notes: Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and V.M. Pancholi. The court issued show-cause notices to the Chief Secretary and others. The state government apologised and said there was no wilful disobedience. The BJP attacked the TVK government; the DMK blamed the state's legal department.

items.text: US Trade Representative [[p:Jamieson Greer]] said Indian goods would face a 17% tariff cap under a trade deal and up to 25% without one; the new tariffs go to public consultation before taking effect next year. On 27 Nov, Commerce Minister [[p:Piyush Goyal]] said the deal is nearing completion and differences are being resolved. The same week the US proposed tariffs of up to 20% on 14 economies, India among them, over alleged excess production.
items.notes: India and the US reached an interim framework in February. Finance Minister Sitharaman said in October that talks had hit a plateau.

items.text: On PM [[p:Balen Shah]]'s first official visit to India, the two governments signed eight MoUs and issued a joint vision document. Modi announced an assistance package of NPR 240bn (about $1.6bn): NPR 56bn in grants for reconstruction after the Bhotekoshi floods and NPR 184bn in concessional credit. Nepal had asked for NPR 100bn in grants and NPR 100bn in loans. India agreed to two-way flights on the Bhairahawa–Lucknow air route, and the joint statement asked foreign secretaries to handle boundary field inspections and pillar maintenance.
items.notes: Neither leader raised the Lipulekh/Kalapani dispute in public. Former PM Pushpa Kamal Dahal reportedly called the visit routine. The Kandla and Paradip ports were offered for transit.

items.text: A spokesperson for [[p:Sheikh Hasina]], who is in exile in India, said she plans to return on 16 Dec (Victory Day) and asked the [[p:Tarique Rahman]] government to arrange her flight from Delhi. The government's press secretary said it will keep seeking her extradition as a convicted person. Junior foreign minister Humaiun Kobir said she could return only in handcuffs or under strict surveillance.
items.notes: Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia. According to a prosecutor, she missed the deadline to appeal and has not sought clemency.

items.text: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the banned [[p:Awami League]] has become a terrorist organisation and will never return to democratic politics. He dismissed Hasina's announced return dates, saying any return would require extradition. He said several police officers had been arrested on sedition charges over alleged political bias, and that border guards were deployed to areas at risk of unrest before Victory Day.
items.notes: The Election Commission has suspended the party's registration. A formal ban is going through the courts under the International Crimes (Tribunals) (Amendment) Act, 2026.

items.text: Awami League ward leader Abdul Halim Sheikh was shot dead by two men on a motorcycle in Khulna's Daulatpur; police have not identified a motive. Khulna police count 81 killings in the district and city this year. Local reports say attackers burned more than 50 homes and shops of Awami League members in Narail's Kalia on 20 Nov; the party says officials are downplaying the arson.
items.notes: Both links carry IANS copy, which cites bdnews24 and Khulna police, so this is not an independent cross-check. The shooting took place on Tuesday night (24 Nov).

items.text: A garment-sector wage board voted 4–2 to set the minimum monthly wage at Tk 17,000, up 36%. Workers had asked for Tk 18,000 and owners had offered Tk 15,700. Some union leaders rejected the figure and protests continued outside the wage board. [[p:Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association|BGMEA]] figures showed 397 factories closed a day earlier, and workers blocked the Dhaka–Mymensingh highway in Gazipur.
items.notes: Unrest has lasted nearly a month. Earlier demands were as high as Tk 30,000. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused some groups of exploiting the protests politically.

items.text: The 91st meeting of the Bangladesh–India joint committee on the 1996 Ganges water treaty ended in Dhaka after finalising the 2026 implementation report. Officials said it had no mandate to discuss renewal, and India has set no date for talks. Bangladesh wants a new deal restoring a guaranteed minimum flow like the one in the 1977 accord; its water resources minister wrote to his Indian counterpart on 17 Nov. The treaty expires on 12 Dec.
items.notes: The treaty can be renewed only by mutual consent. Analysts have floated a three-to-five-year interim extension, but neither government has proposed one. Without a deal, the January 2027 dry season would start with no formal water-sharing arrangement.

items.text: [[p:S&P Global Ratings]] raised Sri Lanka's sovereign rating from CCC+ to B- with a stable outlook. It cited higher revenue, reserves of $7.09bn in October and continued reform under the IMF programme, which ends in March 2027. It flagged energy-price pressure from the Middle East war, slowing remittances, weaker tourism earnings and a possible El Niño in 2027.
items.notes: S&P projects net government debt at about 92% of GDP in 2026 and interest payments at about 40% of revenue.

items.text: The Teachers and Principals Trade Union Alliance called an island-wide one-day sick-leave strike for 30 Nov after talks with PM [[p:Harini Amarasuriya]] failed to resolve pay grievances left out of the 2027 budget. On 27 Nov the Government Medical Officers' Association said it would support the action.
items.notes: The unions say about 250,000 educators are involved. Ceylon Teachers' Union general secretary Joseph Stalin warned of further action. According to a Daily Mirror headline, President Dissanayake called the salary protests a planned conspiracy and promised Rs 150bn for salaries from the 2028 budget; that article was not read in full.

items.text: The opposition [[p:Maldivian Democratic Party]] held a rally at Malé's Artificial Beach demanding a referendum before the government allocates 500 hectares of Ras Malé to UAE developer Eagle Hills. Party chair [[p:Mohamed Nasheed]] said his own government erred by not holding a referendum before awarding the airport contract to India's GMR in 2010, and warned against selling state assets below value to service debt.
items.notes: Nasheed says he supports the project itself but wants a public vote. President Muizzu has ruled out a referendum. The MDP is split into factions ahead of its National Council elections, and some members have joined separate anti-project rallies led by Imran Abdulla's National Movement.

items.text: The [[p:Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] and the [[p:Shiromani Akali Dal]] announced in New Delhi that they are renewing their alliance ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly election. The two parties split in 2020 over the farm laws.
items.notes: This comes from a daily news roundup. Seat-sharing terms were not given; earlier reports had the BJP seeking 47–48 seats.

items.text: [[p:Nikol Pashinyan]] presented a draft new constitution, which the Justice Ministry published for public comment. The draft drops the preamble's reference to the 1990 Declaration of Independence, which Azerbaijan has made a condition for signing the peace treaty. It also sets up vetting of sitting judges, introduces jury trials and lets courts strip citizenship for crimes against state security. A referendum needs 70 of 105 MPs; [[p:Civil Contract (Armenia)|Civil Contract]] has 64, and the opposition factions reject the draft as a concession to Baku.
items.notes: Asia Daily reports that Azerbaijani FM Bayramov welcomed the draft's apparent lack of territorial claims while calling its timing Armenia's internal affair (single source). AP says the draft is cut to 89 articles and widens presidential powers. Justice Minister Galyan said on 26 Nov that the coat of arms with Mount Ararat would not change. Yerepouni and AP agree that no referendum date has been set.

items.text: Economy Minister Gevorg Papoyan said Armenia will ask the [[p:Eurasian Economic Union]] court for an advisory opinion on Russia's restrictions on Armenian goods. The bloc's board postponed its own review of the issue to 1 Dec. Pashinyan will visit Moscow on 3 Dec, and a meeting with [[p:Vladimir Putin]] has been agreed; he said he wants the dispute settled within the bloc.
items.notes: Russia has restricted many Armenian products since early 2026, which is widely seen as linked to Yerevan's EU-membership law; Pashinyan ruled out repealing that law. The Kremlin expects him to say whether he will attend the informal CIS summit in St Petersburg on 22 Dec.

items.text: In the [[p:Georgian Dream]] suit to ban five opposition parties, [[p:Constitutional Court of Georgia|Constitutional Court]] chairman Revaz Nadaraia ordered [[p:Nika Gvaramia]] of the Coalition for Change out of the hearing after Gvaramia accused the judges of siding with the plaintiff. It was his second expulsion in the case. The coalition's representatives did not return after a break and were barred from questioning the plaintiff. The hearing was adjourned to 30 Nov after a death in one judge's family.
items.notes: link2 (Georgia Today) covers his first expulsion on 11 Nov and the court's refusal to delay any ban to allow an ECHR appeal.

items.text: The [[p:European Parliament]] voted 441–47, with 86 abstentions, for a resolution condemning the prison sentences of opera singer Paata Burchuladze and two co-defendants over the 4 Oct 2025 rally. It calls for the release of all political prisoners and EU sanctions on senior officials, judges and prosecutors, including [[p:Bidzina Ivanishvili]]. Deputy Foreign Minister Giorgi Zurabashvili said the resolution spreads false information about Georgia.
items.notes: A Tbilisi court sentenced Burchuladze to seven years earlier in 2026, according to OperaWire and Caspian Post coverage found in search; Burchuladze denies the charges.

items.text: Giorgi Zurabashvili, Georgia's new special representative for Russia, said that at his first meeting with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin in Minsk on 19 Nov, Russia did not lift its bans on Georgian drinks and instead said two more wine producers would be restricted. On 27 Nov [[p:Irakli Kobakhidze]] asked Moscow to review the bans, calling them baseless, and repeated that diplomatic ties cannot resume while Russia occupies Georgian territory. [[p:Sergei Lavrov]] said Moscow wants to normalise relations.
items.notes: Russia restricted imports from seven Georgian beverage producers in October. Zurabashvili, speaking on Imedi TV, said Galuzin cited product quality, funding of Ukraine's war effort and anti-Russian rhetoric, and offered no evidence for any of them. JAMnews says other sources have not confirmed the two new bans.

items.text: Azerbaijan and Lithuania signed a strategic partnership declaration in Baku during Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys's visit. Lithuania pledged to push EU–Azerbaijan visa-easing talks during its EU Council presidency in the first half of 2027. Estonia opened an embassy in Baku the next day.
items.notes: This week the same JAMnews feed reports that a Milli Majlis committee considered the NGO bill letting the executive suspend NGOs for up to a year; it found no final vote (see W-261121-12).

items.text: [[p:Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] met Putin in the Kremlin during a 25–26 Nov working visit, which included a Sberbank AI conference in Moscow. Tokayev said trade is nearing $30bn and that 124 of 178 projects from Putin's May state visit are complete. Putin said over 90% of payments are in national currencies. No new agreements were announced.
items.notes: Tokayev also congratulated Putin on the Shenzhen summit with Xi and Trump, per Akorda. Trend reports Russia–Kazakhstan trade of $20.85bn in Jan–Sep 2026.

items.text: Former industry minister Yersaiyn Nagaspayev took over the state railway [[p:Kazakhstan Temir Zholy]], whose previous chief is in pre-trial custody with the head of [[p:Samruk-Kazyna]]. Samruk-Kazyna said banks advising on the railway's IPO recommended delaying it to 2027. HSBC has waived a breach of a loan covenant until 30 Nov.
items.notes: On 16 Nov Tokayev also replaced security chief Yermek Sagimbayev with his deputy Marat Irmenov without giving a reason (Times of Central Asia, Askar Kubaizhanov). The Times of Central Asia also reported on 25 Nov that a Kazatomprom executive was detained in the probe; that article could not be fetched.

items.text: A consortium led by [[p:Todd Boehly]]'s Eldridge, including the US International Development Finance Corporation, agreed to buy [[p:Lukoil]]'s international arm, which holds the sanctioned Russian company's foreign assets. The Times of Central Asia says the deal could reshape Kazakhstan's oil sector, where Lukoil holds stakes in major projects. It needs US Treasury approval, which Boehly said could take up to a year.
items.notes: Citing Reuters, the article says payment would be about $10bn in Russian securities, against a portfolio sources value at about $16bn. The Reuters original has not been checked separately.

items.text: Klara Sooronkulova became the fifth of 11 presidential hopefuls to pass the 30,000-signature threshold, after President [[p:Sadyr Japarov]] (60,000), Iskhak Masaliev, Aimen Kasenov and Syimyk Zhapykeev. Signature collection ends on 8 Dec.
items.notes: Economist.kg (Aziza Kapar kyzy) gives 7 Dec as the signature deadline; 24.kg says 8 Dec. Translated from Russian.

items.text: Tajikistan notified the UN of its withdrawal from the [[p:International Criminal Court]]; it takes effect on 20 Nov 2027. The notification came on the day [[p:Emomali Rahmon]] hosted Putin, who is under an ICC arrest warrant. Al Jazeera says Tajikistan is the fourth country to start leaving since Washington urged states in July to quit the court.
items.notes: According to The Insider, parliament approved the exit in October, and Deputy FM Idibek Kalandar cited the court's politicisation. In March the ICC found that Tajikistan had failed to arrest Putin during his 2025 visit. Al Jazeera notes the ICC governing body's concern. Reported publicly on 23–24 Nov.

items.text: On [[p:Shavkat Mirziyoyev]]'s state visit to Amman, Uzbekistan and Jordan upgraded ties to a strategic partnership and signed 19 documents, covering legal assistance in criminal matters, energy and water. The two sides set a $500m trade target.

Uzbekistan and Switzerland signed an agreement to return a further $252.5m confiscated from [[p:Gulnara Karimova]]. The money goes through the UN-backed Ishonch 2030 trust fund for health and education. The same day, the [[p:World Bank]] board approved an $800m reform package for Uzbekistan, after S&P raised the country's rating to BB+ on 21 Nov.
items.outlet: Gazeta.uz (citing the Ministry of Economy and Finance)
items.notes: About $313m was returned in earlier stages (2022 and 2025). The Times of Central Asia also reported the asset return.

items.text: Turkmenistan's parliament unanimously passed the 2027 state budget without disclosing revenue or spending totals. In September the IMF board found Turkmenistan in breach of its membership obligations for not providing required data.

An analysis of leaked Russian state statistics (Rosstat) records by the Dossier Center and the New Eurasian Strategies Centre identified 4,091 Central Asians believed to have died fighting for Russia since February 2022: 1,375 from Kazakhstan, 1,301 from Uzbekistan, 831 from Tajikistan, 415 from Kyrgyzstan and 169 from Turkmenistan. The researchers say the records are incomplete.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: The data come from a hack by Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow announced on 1 Nov. JAMnews (25 Nov) separately reports that 408 Azerbaijani citizens were killed fighting for Russia.
